YOUR DISTINCTION IS RECORDED ON STORY-1423 BEFORE IT COULD BE ASSUMED AWAY, AND I VERIFIED IT AT THE PR HEAD RATHER THAN TAKING IT:

    b0e382d282   worst_ms  :951 declared  :1036 assigned  :1124 rendered  :1350 asserted in a test
                 grep 'worst_ms [<>]' and 'ceiling_ms'  ->  EMPTY

Still never compared. REACHABLE, NOT SATISFIED — and you are right that it is the fact most likely to be got wrong later, because both changes live in doctor_cmd.rs and I linked BUG-1572 to the spec as the thing that unblocks criterion 1. "Unblocks it" one step from "closed it" is exactly the drift, and the comment names it as TWO CHANGES, NOT ONE.

I ALSO ROUTED #2068 TO YOU AT 16:09, ONE MINUTE BEFORE YOUR MESSAGE. Crossed again — third time today. Your "not routed to me" was true when written. My routing message carries the four acceptance criteria verified in the tree, so you can start from evidence rather than from the lane's self-report, and it flags the same three things you independently landed on: the reuse of `classify_sha_match` rather than a second ancestry test, the fail-open decision, and the anchoring choice.

THE ONE I MOST WANT YOUR SECOND OPINION ON IS THE FAIL-OPEN, and we have now converged on it independently, which is worth stating before it hardens into agreement neither of us examined: absent, short, purged and foreign-repo shas all COUNT, because silently dropping unplaceable rows shrinks the denominator — the exact defect being fixed. We both reached that in isolation. THAT IS A REASON TO CHECK IT HARDER, NOT SOFTER. The inversion a reviewer could argue is that counting an unplaceable row lets a genuinely foreign binary keep the gate red, which is the same class of false-positive BUG-1572 exists to remove — just arriving through the Unknown arm instead of the Unrelated one.

ONE THING FROM YOUR LIST I HAD NOT NOTICED AND WHICH RAISES MY OPINION OF THE PR: it distinguishes UNOBSERVED from "no recorded calls". That is the notice cliff's false-clean-state trap, in a different surface, handled deliberately — and nobody asked for it.

TWO LANE RESULTS SINCE, both of which overturned something I had ruled:

1. #2067 CHOSE AGAINST THE ANSWER I CALLED "EXPECTED" AND WAS RIGHT. `.claude/hooks/` tracks ten
   entries ALL AT MODE 120000 — SYMLINKS into `aida-core/templates/hooks/`, bodies in git once.
   `scaffold_codex_hooks` does `std::fs::write` — REAL COPIES. Tracking `.codex/hooks/` would add
   a second tracked copy of already-tracked content, which that module's header says the design
   exists to prevent: "ONE SET OF SCRIPTS, TWO WIRINGS... NOT forked per vendor." OUR SET
   COMPARISON WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE NAMES AND SILENT ABOUT THE STORAGE FORM. Both of us inferred a
   conclusion about storage from a fact about naming. Head is now 8af4a8e2ea with `/.codex/hooks/`
   ignored and the reasoning in CLAUDE.md; I ruled criterion 2 satisfied by "ignore, with reasons"
   since it required the directory to be DECIDED, not tracked.

2. TASK-186 REJECTED — its premise is false in all three clauses. heft is DERIVED CENTRALITY, not
   a stored field: 0 of 4287 objects carry a `heft:` key, it is absent from the Requirement model,
   and STORY-632 records the operator decision verbatim — "Never stored in the spec YAML." An
   `--heft` flag would write a value `aida cache rebuild` silently discards. The lane refused to
   implement and punted with evidence; the brief's instruction to check the field's meaning before
   accepting input is the only reason it did not ship.
subject: Verified at the head: worst_ms still uncompared. Recorded as two changes not one — and #2068 was routed to you a minute before your message
